title: actual published main comparator (origin/main at start)
wording:
The RETD (Beckham Law) is available to individuals who:
1. Become Spanish tax residents due to **moving to Spain for work**
2. Have **not been Spanish tax resident in the 5 years** prior to arrival
3. Are employed by a Spanish company or posted to Spain by a foreign employer, OR
   (since 2023 reform) are:
   - Remote workers for foreign companies ("digital nomads")
   - Entrepreneurs starting a business in Spain
   - Highly qualified professionals working for "emerging companies"
   - Individuals managing qualified investment in Spain

destination: Current LF15 Metadata; source-checked reconciliation, not an exact old unit. See disposition note.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: Calculate the 2026 art. 93 special regime, commonly called the Beckham regime, only after documenting eligibility and election. This revision is sourced from the law; independent whole-pack review is pending and no accountant has signed it off.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: ## Who this applies to

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: [LIRPF art. 93](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a93) lets qualifying individuals who become Spanish tax resident because of moving to Spain elect the special IRNR computation **while remaining IRPF taxpayers**. The move must meet a statutory work, administrator, entrepreneur or highly qualified professional route, and occur in the first application year or the preceding year. The individual must not have been Spanish resident during the five tax periods before the move. The professional-athlete special employment relationship is excluded.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: Qualifying employment includes a Spanish employment/statutory relationship, an employer-directed posting evidenced by its letter, or employment performed remotely using the specified IT/telecommunications means. The international telework visa supports the employment route; a visa does not dispense with the remaining tax conditions. Ordinary freelance work is not automatically qualifying remote **employment**.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: An administrator can qualify, but an administrator of a patrimonial entity must not hold a participation that makes them related under LIS art. 18. Entrepreneurial activity requires the [RIRPF art. 113.2](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a113) ENISA/residence-authorisation evidence. Highly qualified services to qualifying emerging companies or the specified training/research/development/innovation activity require the same article's evidence and art. 93.1.b.4's **more-than-40%** remuneration condition. No Spanish PE income is allowed except in the expressly permitted entrepreneur/highly-qualified activity routes. Do not classify every investment manager or self-employed digital nomad as eligible.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: Before electing, check **RIRPF article 116.3**: a taxpayer who has used the special incoming-worker employment-withholding procedure in **article 89.B cannot exercise this special-regime option**. Article 89.B concerns an employee anticipating ordinary Spanish IRPF withholding on a move to Spain; AEAT identifies that communication as **Modelo 147**. It is a different procedure from the Modelo 149 special-regime election. Retain the actual prior communication, AEAT accreditation and payer implementation evidence rather than assuming that a timely 149 overrides the bar. [RIRPF arts.89.B/116.3](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a116); [AEAT general incoming-worker procedure/Modelo147](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/irpf/tengo-que-presentar-declaracion/regimen-fiscal-aplicable-trabajadores-desplazados.html).

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: For example, an employee otherwise meets the article 93 residence-history, move and employment conditions and remains within the six-month election deadline, but has already used article 89.B's special withholding procedure. Article 116.3 bars the election on those facts. Absence of that prior procedure only clears this additional gate; every other eligibility/election condition still applies. The article89.A passive-benefit withholding procedure is a separately named procedure, so do not broaden the specific89.B bar by analogy.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: Qualifying spouse/children under 25, disabled children of any age, or the specified unmarried co-parent can elect individually under art. 93.3. Check their move/residence timing, five-year non-residence history, prohibited-PE condition and the annual **combined associated bases strictly below the principal's base**. [RIRPF art. 113.3](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a113) addresses an associated person's earlier arrival without earlier tax residence than the principal's first regime year. A family relationship alone does not grant automatic treatment.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
section: ## The base / ### Identify Spanish-source income correctly
wording: Under [LIRPF art. 93.2.b](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a93), **all employment income and income from a qualifying entrepreneurial activity obtained during the regime is deemed Spanish-source**. Foreign work, employer, payroll or bank account does not by itself exclude it. [RIRPF art. 114.2.a](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a114) excludes from that deeming rule income attributable to activity **before the move** or **after the notified end of the posting**, without removing any independently Spanish-source income under IRNR rules. Allocate a bonus/award by the underlying service period and keep the evidence.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
section: ## The base / ### Identify Spanish-source income correctly
wording: For other income, apply [TRLIRNR art. 13](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527#a13). A genuinely foreign-source passive dividend, interest receipt, property rent or gain is not automatically brought into this special Spanish base. A foreign account can hold Spanish-source income, so its location is not the source test. Conversely, Spanish-property rent and other Spanish-source ordinary income enter the non-savings category unless the statute puts them in art. 25.1.f's savings category. Spanish-source dividends, interest and transfer gains use that separate savings-category scale.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
section: ## The base / ### Identify Spanish-source income correctly
wording: Apply the IRNR base rules as modified by art. 93: ordinary employment is gross income, without automatically importing the annual resident employee-expense deduction or personal/family minimum. Art. 93.2.a disapplies the enumerated IRNR provisions, including general art. 14 exemptions except the specified exempt in-kind employment. Do not add ordinary IRPF exemptions/reliefs merely because the individual remains an IRPF taxpayer ([LIRPF art. 93.2](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a93); [TRLIRNR art. 24](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527#a24)).

wording: 5. For foreign employment/qualifying entrepreneurial income, calculate the [LIRPF art. 80](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a80) foreign-tax credit, then enforce the additional **30% of work/entrepreneur quota** cap in RIRPF art. 114.2.b. The effective-rate computation excludes both savings base and savings quota. In a salary-only ordinary category, the ceiling is `min(qualifying_foreign_tax, foreign_work_income ×ordinary_tax/O, 0.30 ×ordinary_tax)`. With mixed ordinary-category income, first attribute the quota to all qualifying work/entrepreneur income; do not take 30% of unrelated property tax or the savings quota.

wording: For professional economic activity, [RIRPF art. 114.3](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a114) limits withholding to activities classified as professional under its special rule and requires the applicable rate on invoices. wording: An NIE alone does not start or satisfy the election. Retain the actual qualifying activity date and submitted election/accreditation. wording: For associated people, loss of the combined-base condition or the principal's renunciation/exclusion excludes the associated group as provided in art. 118.4; other individual eligibility failures can exclude only the affected member. wording: ## Penalties and interest

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: An unprompted late 151 with tax due follows [LGT art. 27](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186#a27): generally 1% plus 1% per complete month through twelve months, then 15% plus the specified subsequent interest, with the article's conditions/reductions. Under-declared tax or a required information communication follows its own [arts. 191/198/199](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186#a191) classification. A penalty or surcharge payment does not itself establish substantive eligibility for a missed election. Use [LGT arts. 26/28](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186#a26) for actual interest and collection stage, not an invented fixed fee for every late communication.

wording: ## Cross-border points

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: The central cross-border distinction is **source and service period**, not the currency or payer account. Worldwide employment during the regime is within the deeming rule; genuinely foreign-source passive income needs the separate IRNR source test. Foreign work tax can produce only the bounded credit above, not an automatic exemption. Obtain actual foreign assessments and the attributable service-income schedule.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
wording: A tax visa is not the regime election, and an A1/origin-coverage document is not proof of a tax exemption. Establish treaty entitlement, social security and this domestic election separately. On leaving, review art. 119.5 notification, the remaining residence year, source rules for later payments and potential [LIRPF art. 95 bis](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a95bis) exit-tax residence-history rules, including its special-regime counting provision. Do not infer no departure obligations merely because the six-year election ended.

title: frozen GitHub-public PR branch body
section: ## Two worked examples that recompute / ### 1. Employment abroad remains included, foreign passive dividend does not automatically enter
wording: A hypothetical valid elector has **110,000 gross employment income for services performed during the 2026 regime**, including 20,000 for work physically abroad. No qualifying foreign tax was paid. A Spanish-source dividend is 4,000; a separate 5,000 dividend is established to be genuinely foreign-source under art. 13. Include the whole 110,000 employment, ordinary tax **26,400**, plus Spanish-dividend tax **760**, total **27,160** before supported payments on account. The foreign dividend is outside this special Spanish source base; the foreign-work salary is included. No ordinary employee-expense or personal-minimum deduction is assumed ([LIRPF art. 93](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a93); [RIRPF art. 114](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a114)).

section: ## Two worked examples that recompute / ### 1. Employment abroad remains included, foreign passive dividend does not automatically enter
wording:
```oa-check
name: Spain 2026 impatriate employment-source deeming and passive source
inputs:
  spanish_work_salary: 90000
  foreign_work_salary: 20000
  spanish_dividend: 4000
  foreign_source_dividend: 5000
steps:
  employment_base: spanish_work_salary + foreign_work_salary
  ordinary_tax: min(employment_base, 600000) * 0.24 + max(employment_base - 600000, 0) * 0.47
  savings_tax: spanish_dividend * 0.19
  excluded_foreign_passive: foreign_source_dividend
  total_gross_tax: ordinary_tax + savings_tax
expected:
  employment_base: 110000
  ordinary_tax: 26400
  savings_tax: 760
  excluded_foreign_passive: 5000
  total_gross_tax: 27160
```

section: ## Two worked examples that recompute / ### 2. Two employers, top savings band and foreign-credit cap
wording: A hypothetical valid full-year elector receives **650,000 employment**, half from each of two payers, all for services during the regime. Of it, 300,000 relates to work abroad with 80,000 qualifying foreign tax. Spanish-source dividends are 310,000, with no loss or donation deduction. Ordinary tax is **167,500**; savings tax **74,880**. The salary-only effective-rate foreign-income limit is 77,307.69, but the extra 30%-of-employment-quota limit restricts credit to **50,250**. Tax after credit is **192,130**. Each salary payer paid only 325,000 and withheld 24%, total 156,000; dividend withholding at the IRNR 19% rate is 58,900. With supported credits of 214,900, the return balance is **−22,770**, a refund. The result tests annual aggregation, payer-specific withholding and the additional credit cap ([LIRPF art. 93.2.e/f](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a93); [RIRPF art. 114.2.b](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6820#a114); [TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527#a25)).
